## Introduction

Tipping is one of the few everyday transactions where the customer decides the price, which makes it a useful window into how people handle money. This paper asks whether the total bill is correlated with the tip, and therefore whether diners scale their generosity to the size of the meal.

## Literature Review

The (entirely fictional) Guild of Weary Waiters has long claimed that "a big table brings a big tip," a theory drawn mostly from stories told after closing time. The rival Society of Skeptical Diners counters that tips are driven by mood, weather, and how often the water glass was refilled, though neither group has ever opened a spreadsheet to check.

## Method

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

df = sns.load_dataset("tips")

n = len(df)
mean_bill = df["total_bill"].mean()
mean_tip = df["tip"].mean()
mean_tip_pct = (df["tip"] / df["total_bill"]).mean() * 100
```

The sample includes `{python} f"{n}"` restaurant bills, with an average bill of $`{python} f"{mean_bill:.2f}"`, an average tip of $`{python} f"{mean_tip:.2f}"`, and an average tip rate of `{python} f"{mean_tip_pct:.1f}"`%. A Pearson correlation tests the null hypothesis that total bill and tip are unrelated (ρ = 0) against the alternative that they are correlated (ρ ≠ 0).

## Results

```{python}
corr_matrix = df.corr(numeric_only=True)

r = corr_matrix.loc["total_bill", "tip"]

r_check, pval = stats.pearsonr(df["total_bill"], df["tip"])
degf = n - 2
r_sq_pct = r**2 * 100

p_text = "p < .001" if pval < 0.001 else f"p = {pval:.3f}"

corr_matrix.round(2)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Total bill and tip, with a fitted regression line."
sns.regplot(data=df, x="total_bill", y="tip", scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.6})
plt.xlabel("Total bill ($)")
plt.ylabel("Tip ($)")
plt.show()
```

Total bill and tip were significantly and positively correlated, r(`{python} f"{degf}"`) = `{python} f"{r:.2f}"`, `{python} p_text`. The size of the bill accounts for about `{python} f"{r_sq_pct:.0f}"`% of the variation in tips (see @fig-scatter), leaving the rest to other factors.

## Discussion

These results reject the null hypothesis and suggest that diners do scale their tips to the size of the bill, broadly supporting the Guild of Weary Waiters. However, the data come from a single server over a few months, so future research should test whether the pattern holds across restaurants and regions, and whether party size, time of day, or smoking section explain the remaining variation.
